description: P2-08b unified bitFlyer FX_BTC_JPY execution series, 2026-07-23..2026-09-06, one UTC-microsecond schema across the two raw sources this repo holds (REST 31-day snapshot, WS tape recording). Built by scripts/normalize_bitflyer_executions.py. Primary-source rule follows PREREG.md's calendar seal boundary: days 2026-07-23..2026-08-22 use the REST snapshot (real execution ids), days 2026-08-23..2026-09-06 use the WS tape (no execution id carried by that extraction -- left blank). See overlap_check.csv for a day-by-day cross-check of the days both sources cover (2026-08-20..2026-08-23).
source: backtest_data/executions_FX_BTC_JPY_31d_20260823.csv.gz (REST /v1/getexecutions frozen snapshot, ms exchange timestamp) + paper_logs/tape/executions_YYYYMMDD.csv.gz (WS lightning_executions_FX_BTC_JPY recording extracted by scripts/extract_tape.py, exchange timestamp at native sub-ms precision). Combined by scripts/normalize_bitflyer_executions.py.
retention: permanent, dated snapshot for reproducibility; not appended forward (the input sources themselves keep growing independently -- re-run the script to rebuild a fresher window).

id.meaning: bitFlyer execution id, REST days only
id.notes: blank for every row on WS-primary days (2026-08-23 onward) -- the WS tape extraction (scripts/extract_tape.py) does not carry an execution id at all, see schema/bitflyer_tape.json's own note on the same limitation

ts_us.meaning: EXCHANGE execution timestamp, normalized to UTC microseconds
ts_us.notes: REST source is natively millisecond precision (x1000 here, trailing 3 digits always zero); WS source is natively sub-millisecond (commonly 7 fractional digits as bitFlyer sends it, truncated to microsecond precision here)

source.meaning: which raw source this day's rows came from
source.notes: one value for the WHOLE day, per the calendar cutover rule above -- not a per-row mixed selection

quality._unique_key_note: id is only a real unique key on 'rest' days; on 'ws' days id is blank for every row (composite (ts_us, price, size, side) is the closest practical key, and is still probabilistic -- see schema/bitflyer_tape.json)

date.notes: only days where BOTH the REST snapshot and a WS tape file exist, i.e. 2026-08-20..2026-08-23

overlap_start_utc.meaning: start of the intersection of REST's and WS's actual timestamp range that day
overlap_start_utc.notes: clips a partial-coverage day (WS starts mid-day on 2026-08-20; REST ends mid-day on 2026-08-23) so the count comparison is apples-to-apples

ws_count_in_window.meaning: WS row count within the same window

ws_drop_rate_pct.notes: the headline 'WS 欠け率' figure quoted in README.md (~0.6-2.8% across the 4 overlap days). A per-trade composite-key match was tried first and rejected -- see the code comment in scripts/normalize_bitflyer_executions.py: bitFlyer's REST and WS execution feeds split partial fills at different granularity, so an exact (ts, price, size, side) key match spuriously reports ~70% mismatch on the SAME trades. This same-window row-count comparison instead reproduces the audit's own cited figures.

gap_start_utc.meaning: timestamp of the last execution before the gap

gap_end_utc.meaning: timestamp of the first execution after the gap

is_maintenance_window.meaning: whether the gap overlaps bitFlyer's documented daily maintenance window (18:59-19:12 UTC)
is_maintenance_window.notes: false entries are the ones worth investigating as real outages (see README.md for the two known multi-hour WS recorder outages in this window)

known_defects: WS-primary days (2026-08-23 onward) carry no execution id at all -- id is blank by construction, not a data-quality gap

the REST<->WS overlap check uses a millisecond-bucket composite key, not a true id join -- both rest_only_count and ws_only_count can include a small number of key-collision artifacts, not only genuine misses

known WS recorder outages within the 2026-08-23..2026-09-06 window (see gaps.csv, is_maintenance_window=false rows): the home-PC WS recorder stopped for multi-hour stretches on at least two occasions -- these show as real gaps in the unified series, not bitFlyer-side maintenance
a second with zero rows in this series is 'no observation', not 'price unchanged' -- consistent with the same convention used for the Binance klines/aggTrades side of P2-08b
